p: speak thou the things which become: The fifth admonition: the doctrine must not only be generally pure, but also be applied to all ages and orders of men, according to the diversity of circumstances.
That the aged men be sober: What are the principal virtues for old and young, both men and women: and how they ought to be stirred up to do them continually.
keepers at home: Not roving about idly.
In all things shewing thyself a: The sixth admonition: that both the pastor's life and doctrine must be sound.
gravity: Not such a gravity as may drive men from coming to the minister, but such as may cause them to come in a most reverent and honest way.
Exhort servants to be obedient unto: The seventh admonition, concerning the duty of servants to their masters.
things: Which may be done without offence to God.

For the grace of God that: The eighth admonition belongs to all the godly: seeing that God calls all men to the Gospel, and Christ has so justified us, that he has also sanctified us, all of us must therefore give ourselves to true godliness, and righteousness, setting before us a sure hope of that immeasurable glory. And this thing must be so learned by them that the deniers also must be reproved, by the authority of the mighty God.
worldly lusts: Lusts of the flesh, which belong to the present state of this life and world.
Looking for that blessed hope: Christ is here most plainly called that mighty God, and his appearance and coming is called by the figure of speech metonymy, our hope.
peculiar people: As it were a thing peculiarly laid aside for himself.
